findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: 1) Observed raw chicken and bacon in the walk in cooler stored above celerey and cheese. 2) Observed raw chicken and beef stored above cooked chicken wings in the reach in cooler. Raw chicken was moved during the inspection so that raw foods were not stored above ready to eat foods. 3-302.11  (P)  Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed nine portions of cheese/queso sitting on top of the lids of items in the steam table that were probed at 115F. Employee states that when they are busy, they pull these to warm up before they microwave them to serve. He states they pull these and use within 10 minutes but is not keeping any documentation of this. These were discarded and hot holding was discussed. 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 1) Observed hot dogs with a date of 3/15 in the prep cooler. 2) Observed coleslaw, cooked onion/peppers and spinach dip with no date and an avocado mix dated 3/15 in the reach in cooler. 3) Observed hot dogs dated 3/15 in the walk in cooler. These are all open, ready to eat foods that must be date marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum with the date of opening/prep counting as a full Day 1. These items were discarded.  3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: Observed a bucket of road salt near the door that was not labeled with the name of the product. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed traditional chicken wings in a bucket cooling in the reach in cooler to be probed at 125F and boneless wings in this same cooler to be probed at 95F with no indication as to when the cooling process began. Cooling must be done rapidly as an active process where it is documented when the cooling process begins to ensure that foods are reaching 70F within 2 hours of cooling. Facility has thermometers available and will begin tracking this. 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: REPEAT PRACTICE> Observed a couple wet wiping cloths sitting on prep surfaces and cloths in the sanitizer bucket to not be fully submerged in sanitizer solution. Store wet wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer solution in between use.  3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed small cups being stored in diced tomatoes in the prep cooler and in coleslaw in the reach in cooler. In use utensils should have a handle with the handle stored up and out of the food if stored in the food in between use.  3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.
